summary: A card from Guatemala and the page it opens. The address printed on the card never changes; the page behind it keeps growing, in Spanish first with English under it.
license_note: MIT is the parent repo's grant and covers this page and the project code. The card artwork is the owner's: commissioned by them, excluded from the MIT grant by NOTICE at the repo root, served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/NOTICE.txt. Nothing in this manifest enlarges what NOTICE withholds — to reuse the artwork, ask the owner.
origin: Not a fork and not a repository of its own: /gt/ is a page-project inside mrdirno/vibe-cards (GitHub reports fork=false), the seed repo of this registry, published on that repo's Pages surface. Its MIT is INHERITED from the parent repo's LICENSE, not chosen for it, and it covers the page and the code only. The card came before the page: the four faces were commissioned from Meta AI by the card's owner and arrived finished — src/web/app.js says at the head of the GT-001 template block 'Finished artwork, placed and not rebuilt', 'a card someone has already designed', 'the original was approved' — and NOTICE at the repo root excludes all four from the MIT grant, so being listed makes nothing about the artwork reusable. The faces entered the tree 2026-08-13T04:20:30Z (first commit touching src/web/templates/gt-archive-back.jpg, commits API, anonymous), three days after the repo was created and a few hours AFTER this registry file's first commit at its current path — so on disk the registry is slightly older than this page, while the card's design predates both, and its paper-and-approval history is the owner's, not this file's to reconstruct. Fragment Mono and Instrument Serif are embedded in the page under SIL OFL 1.1 (OFL.txt, repo root and site). The living entries in src/site/gt/entries.json are the project's own on the only authorship record that exists for them (NOTICE's closing section). GT-001 sat in this registry's held list until 2026-08-16, and the standard's own v1.0.1 amendment used /gt/ as the page that met the account-free wish rule while the seed's own landing page failed it.
_note: A page-project's manifest: /gt/ is a surface of mrdirno/vibe-cards, so this file lives at the surface's own url — the network gate fetches <listed url>/wish-it-better.json, which is how two entries in one repo each carry their own level (the /av/ and /collage/ precedent, except those two share one manifest and one level, while this repo publishes two files at two urls: the root declares L1 for the seed, this one declares L0 for this page). L0 because its three clauses hold and no more is claimed: this file is present at the url the card carries, the wish route is the page's own mailto — account-free, with 'no hace falta cuenta ni contraseña' printed under it — and LICENSE at the repo root is real SPDX MIT. Not L1: a wish reaches an inbox, not a queue with recorded terminal states. The wish_channel is deliberately the mailto and not the landing page's wishing well: the well is real but it lives on the seed's page — the route a GT card holder actually has, on the page their chip opens, is this mailto, and the field declares what is real for THIS surface.
